title: Check inherited contribution policy before research intake
applies_when: Adding a public repository to an automated contribution scout, especially when a clone contains no CONTRIBUTING file, rules live in README/PR/agent instructions, AI/human-review rules depend on contributor status, or a technically valid fix may not be publishable.
lesson: Check contributor eligibility before expensive discovery, then recheck before publication. GitHub can inherit rules from the owner's public .github repository, absent from the target clone. Resolve the effective document using its actual public html_url repository, pin and read it; follow linked policies too. Explicitly select named project guides: Pyee's DEVELOPMENT.md requires bot-emoji prefixes for AI-assisted commits/changelog and reviewer disclosure, not a ban. Keep technical correctness, contributor-policy eligibility and current interaction permissions separate. Pallets' linked AI policy specifically excludes AI use by new contributors; established contributors still need genuine personal understanding and authorship, not an agent-issued trust certificate. Tests or a review checkbox do not override such a restriction. The repository metadata GET can cheaply expose archived/disabled state and PR creation policy: has_pull_requests=true does not override collaborators_only. An existing public fork is not an upstream PR. Temporary interaction limits and per-user PR caps are additional, separate constraints. Preserve useful private evidence, respect existing authors' patches, and redirect contribution effort instead of bypassing a restriction.
avoid_when: An absent profile/file, missing setting or failed read is not permission. Also read README contribution sections: a minimal reproduction need not meet a project's separate requirement for actual affected production code. Do not manufacture a production witness. Ordinary exploratory packets should reuse the existing repository question as well as their task-specific question; standalone packets do not inherit it automatically. Do not retrofit this advice into admitted frozen experiment arms. Settings are timestamped observations, not contributor authorization; all does not prove an available per-user quota or permissive written rules. A prior contributor's reported denial is a reason to investigate, not proof that every user remains restricted. Limits can expire and policies can change. Do not transfer an organization's policy elsewhere, infer eligibility from keywords, or treat disclosure/review requirements as blanket bans. Internal reference testing does not authorize externally submitting its AI-generated output. A PR restriction does not by itself forbid bug reports; review the actual issue policy independently. No PR-yield or cost benefit is established by this lesson.

evidence.note: The pinned project guide requires bot-emoji prefixes and AI disclosure. Community-profile documents alone are not a complete guide index; explicit selection still needs review, not automatic permission.

The effective organization guide permits AI-assisted code but requires actual human review and forbids LLM-authored community speech, explicitly including PR descriptions and changelogs except translation/grammar. A passing privately tested repair still needs genuine human review and wording; a generic publish approval is not authorship. This guide is inherited even when the target clone has no CONTRIBUTING file.

This pinned template requires an open issue for nontrivial PRs and tox validation; a raw unittest run is not the requested complete contribution check. Read the actual test recipe before preparing a publication-ready change.

This agent guide carries useful contribution/test rules but also stale implementation claims: it says Python>=3.10 and deprecated cache=None/classmethod paths, while the same revision's pyproject requires >=3.11 and docs describe their removal. Separate workflow requirements from factual architecture summaries; verify the latter against current source and configuration.

This revision puts contribution rules in the README: generally open an issue before a PR, and assistant-found bug reports must show actual affected production code; sanitized examples are permitted but contrived ones are not. This is not a blanket AI ban or evidence that a synthetic reproduction is false.
GitHub documents default community files in the owner's .github repository, their location precedence and why inherited files are not present in individual clones.

The linked policy covers all community interactions, distinguishes new from established trusted contributors, and requires genuine personal understanding and creation. Recheck this live policy before deciding eligibility; do not simplify it to a universal rule for every project or contributor.
GitHub documents temporary interaction restrictions, including collaborator-only participation that can prevent creating PRs independently of a project's written contribution guide.
GitHub separately supports disabling PRs and restricting their creation to collaborators; enabled features and written contribution guides are not a complete access decision.

A release-reproduced concurrency bug has a tested public fork but no upstream PR because creation is collaborators-only. It was submitted through the independently permitted issue channel, not counted as a PR conversion.

Observed on 2026-10-13: the upstream comparison explicitly says its owner disabled opening pull requests. This is a timestamped contribution constraint, not a code-quality verdict; do not infer policy merely from an absent navigation tab.

An existing report links another author's UTF-8/in-place repair in their fork. Independent reproduction or test-fixture feedback can support that work, but cannot be counted as a novel discovery, our PR, or an upstream merge. Check this route before spending on a competing implementation.

This revision requires a maintainer's /approve on a linked bug issue before an external fix PR and declines external feature PRs. It permits discussing reports first. Passing native tests, a personal fork or open PR creation settings are not that approval; choose the issue channel before preparing a publication-ready patch. Recheck the live rule before transfer.
